arxiv-2109-05331.title: Extremal { p , q } \{p,q\} -Animals
arxiv-2109-05331.creator: Greg Malen, Érika Roldán, Rosemberg Toalá-Enríquez
arxiv-2109-05331.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Greg Malen, Érika Roldán, Rosemberg Toalá-Enríquez. An animal is a planar shape formed by attaching congruent regular polygons, known as tiles, along their edges. In this paper, we study extremal animals defined on regular tessellations of the plane. In 1976, Harary and Harborth studied animals in the Euclidean cases, finding extremal values for their vertices, edges, and tiles, when any one of these parameters is fixed. Here, we generalize their results to hyperbolic animals.

arxiv-2203-08140.title: Learning Spatio-Temporal Downsampling for Effective Video Upscaling
arxiv-2203-08140.creator: Xiaoyu Xiang, Yapeng Tian, Vijay Rengarajan, Lucas Young, Bo Zhu, Rakesh Ranjan
arxiv-2203-08140.description: Abstract Downsampling is one of the most basic image processing operations. Improper spatio-temporal downsampling applied on videos can cause aliasing issues such as moiré patterns in space and the wagon-wheel effect in time. Consequently, the inverse task of upscaling a low-resolution, low frame-rate video in space and time becomes a challenging ill-posed problem due to information loss and aliasing artifacts.

arxiv-2308-11535.title: Geodesic congruences in acoustic spacetimes and the role of Raychaudhuri equation
arxiv-2308-11535.creator: Akshat Pandey
arxiv-2308-11535.description: Abstract It has been known that the propagation of sound in fluids can be used to model acoustic spacetimes. These acoustic spacetimes offer analogue models for gravity. We use the Raychaudhuri equation to study the propagation of sound in these fluids, which, via the Eikonal approximation, correspond to null geodesic congruences in the acoustic spacetimes.

arxiv-2411-17987.title: P4-NIDS: High-Performance Network Monitoring and Intrusion Detection in P4
arxiv-2411-17987.creator: Yaying Chen 1, Siamak Layeghy 1, Liam Daly Manocchio 1, Marius Portmann 1
arxiv-2411-17987.description: Abstract This paper presents a high-performance, scalable network monitoring and intrusion detection system (IDS) implemented in P4. The proposed solution is designed for high-performance environments such as cloud data centers, where ultra-low latency, high bandwidth, and resilient infrastructure are essential.

arxiv-2506-05787.title: EASG-Bench: Video Q&A Benchmark with Egocentric Action Scene Graphs
arxiv-2506-05787.creator: Ivan Rodin, Tz-Ying Wu, Kyle Min, Sharath Nittur Sridhar, Antonino Furnari, Subarna Tripathi, Giovanni Maria Farinella, [1ex] University of Catania
arxiv-2506-05787.description: Abstract We introduce EASG-Bench , a question-answering benchmark for egocentric videos where the question-answering pairs are created from spatio-temporally grounded dynamic scene graphs capturing intricate relationships among actors, actions, and objects. We propose a systematic evaluation framework and evaluate several language-only and video large language models (video-LLMs) on this benchmark.

arxiv-2511-10235.title: Dynamic full-field swept-source optical coherence microscope for cellular-resolution, long-depth, and intratissue-activity imaging Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2511-10235.creator: Nobuhisa Tateno, 1 Yue Zhu, 1,2 Suzuyo Komeda, 1 Mahiro Ishikawa, 1 Xibo Wang, 1 Ibrahim Abd El-Sadek, 1,3 Rion Morishita, 1 Atsuko Furukawa, 4 Satoshi Matsusaka, 4 Shuichi Makita, 1,* and Yoshiaki Yasuno 1,**
arxiv-2511-10235.description: Abstract Optical coherence tomography (OCT) microscope (OCM) uses a high-numerical-aperture objective to achieve cellular-level lateral resolution. However, its practical imaging depth range is limited by the depth of focus (DOF). Although computational refocusing can potentially provide sharp images outside the DOF, signal reduction by the confocal effect still limits the imaging depth in practice in point-scanning OCT.

arxiv-2512-14009.title: Scaling solutions for gauge invariant flow equations in dilaton quantum gravity
arxiv-2512-14009.creator: Yadikaer Maitiniyazi, Christof Wetterich, Masatoshi Yamada
arxiv-2512-14009.description: Abstract We investigate the effects of quantum gravity for models of a scalar singlet coupled to the metric. Such models describe inflation for early cosmology and dynamical dark energy for late cosmology. We work within the “variable gravity approximation” keeping in the effective action an arbitrary field dependence for terms with up to two derivatives.

pmc-10664413.creator: Yuki Matsumoto, Ryutaro Shimada, Hidemi Morioka, Yoshihiro Morino, Michel Corban, Juan Miguel Guerrero, Elton Luo
pmc-10664413.description: BackgroundIn recent years, endovascular treatment has emerged as a preferred option for treating long lesions in the superficial femoral artery (SFA), including those classified as Trans-Atlantic Inter-Society Consensus IIC and D. pmc-11546163.title: An Update on Molecular Mechanisms of Scarring—A Narrative Review
pmc-11546163.creator: Michael Kohlhauser, Marcel Mayrhofer, Lars-Peter Kamolz, Christian Smolle
pmc-11546163.description: Fibroblasts, the principal cellular mediators of connective tissue remodeling, play a crucial role in the formation of physiological and pathological scars. Understanding the intricate interplay between fibroblasts and other cellular and molecular components is essential for elucidating the underlying mechanisms driving scar formation.

pmc-11674488.title: Exploring memory-related network via dorsal hippocampus suppression
pmc-11674488.creator: Xu Han, Samuel R Cramer, Dennis C Y Chan, Nanyin Zhang
pmc-11674488.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Memory is a complex brain process that requires coordinated activities in a large-scale brain network. However, the relationship between coordinated brain network activities and memory-related behavior is not well understood. In this study, we investigated this issue by suppressing the activity in the dorsal hippocampus (dHP) using chemogenetics and measuring the corresponding changes in brain-wide resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) and memory behavior in awake rats. We identified an extended brain network contributing to the performance in a spatial memory related task.

pmc-12975782.title: An innovative hierarchical porous oxide surface with enhanced surface area for promoting early-stage bone regeneration potential
pmc-12975782.creator: Chia-Ling Shen, Kuo-Sheng Hung, Hsieh-Tsung Shen, Yu-Sin Jennifer Ou, Jungshan Chang, Chi-Hsun Tsai, Takashi Saito, Yi-Ren Pao, Keng-Liang Ou, Chih-Ming Tsai, Xiaoxia Wei
pmc-12975782.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this study, an innovative hierarchical porous oxide surface (HPOS) with an increased surface area was developed on biomedical 316L stainless steel (SS) implants to promote early bone and implant integration. The surface features and in vivo performance of the HPOS implant were examined using field-emission scanning electron microscopy, nanoindenter, roughness measurement instrument, contact angle goniometer, micro-computed tomography, and histological analysis.
